### Health Analytics with R · Module 08: Reproducible Research & Deployment
***
**Learning objectives**
- Understand Quarto's role in reproducible health research reporting
- Create multi-format Quarto documents (HTML, PDF, Word)
- Build publication-quality figures with embedded captions and cross-references
- Generate programmatic Table 1 with statistical tests
- Apply Quarto callouts, tabs, and interactive elements
- Use Quarto for journal submission workflows

**Estimated time:** 2.5 hours | **Level:** Intermediate | **Libraries:** `ggplot2`, `dplyr`, `tidymodels`, `gt`, `patchwork`

## 1. Setup & Dataset

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(pROC)
library(rsample)
library(broom)
library(gt)
library(fs)

mod08_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod08")
dir.create(mod08_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

col_blue <- "#2563EB"
col_red  <- "#DC2626"
col_green <- "#16A34A"
col_gold <- "#D4A017"

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.line        = element_line(colour = "grey40")
    )
)

set.seed(42)
N <- 2000
df <- tibble(
  patient_id = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N) - 1),
  age        = as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 60, 15), 18), 90)),
  los_days   = as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30)),
  diabetes   = rbinom(N, 1, 0.35),
  hf         = rbinom(N, 1, 0.22),
  smoking    = rbinom(N, 1, 0.25),
  payer      = sample(
    c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay"),
    N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.10)
  )
)
sigmoid <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))
logit <- -3.2 + 0.6 * df$hf + 0.5 * df$diabetes + 0.02 * (df$age - 60) +
  0.2 * as.integer(df$los_days > 7)
df$readmitted <- rbinom(N, 1, sigmoid(logit))
cat(sprintf("Dataset: %d x %d | Readmission rate: %.1f%%\n",
            nrow(df), ncol(df), mean(df$readmitted) * 100))
```

## 2. Quarto Document Structure

A `.qmd` file is a Markdown file with YAML front matter and executable code chunks. This notebook *is* a Quarto document for R: you are looking at the same format you will use for journal-ready reports.

````markdown
---                          # YAML front matter (metadata)
title: "Report Title"
format: html
engine: knitr

## Section                   # Markdown content

```{{r}}
#| label: fig-roc            # Cross-referenceable label
#| fig-cap: "ROC Curve"      # Caption
plot_roc_curve()
```

See @fig-roc for the discrimination results.   # Auto-numbered cross-ref
````

**Key Quarto advantages over R Markdown / notebooks:**
- Clean separation of code and output
- Native multi-format (HTML/PDF/Word) from same source
- Built-in bibliography (`.bib`) support
- Cross-references, callouts, panel layouts
- Version-control friendly (`.qmd` is plain text)
- Knitr engine is first-class for R (`{r}` chunks, `echo`, `cache`, `fig-cap`)

**Chunk options you will use constantly:**

| Option | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `#\| label: fig-roc` | Cross-reference target (`@fig-roc`) |
| `#\| fig-cap:` | Figure caption |
| `#\| tbl-cap:` | Table caption |
| `#\| echo: false` | Hide code in the rendered report |
| `#\| cache: true` | Skip re-running unchanged chunks |
| `#\| fig-width:` / `#\| fig-height:` | Figure size in inches |
| `#\| message: false` | Suppress package startup messages |

## 3. Quarto YAML Front Matter Template

```{r}
# The Quarto document template for health research reports (R / knitr)
fence_r <- paste0(strrep("`", 3), "{r}")
fence_end <- strrep("`", 3)

QMD_TEMPLATE <- paste(
  c(
    "---",
    "title: '30-Day Readmission Analysis Report'",
    "subtitle: 'Health Analytics Division | Fiscal Year 2024'",
    "author:",
    "  - name: Dr. Data Analyst",
    "    affiliation: Health System Analytics",
    "    email: analyst@healthsystem.org",
    "date: today",
    "format:",
    "  html:",
    "    toc: true",
    "    toc-depth: 3",
    "    theme: cosmo",
    "    embed-resources: true",
    "    code-fold: true",
    "    code-summary: 'Show code'",
    "  pdf:",
    "    documentclass: article",
    "    geometry: margin=1in",
    "    toc: true",
    "  docx:",
    "    reference-doc: templates/report_template.docx",
    "execute:",
    "  echo: false",
    "  warning: false",
    "  cache: true",
    "engine: knitr",
    "bibliography: references.bib",
    "---",
    "",
    "## Executive Summary",
    "",
    "::: {.callout-note}",
    "**Key Finding:** 30-day readmission rate was {{< readmit_rate >}}%, with highest risk",
    "among patients with heart failure (OR {{< hf_or >}}, 95% CI {{< hf_ci >}}).",
    ":::",
    "",
    "## Methods",
    "",
    fence_r,
    "#| label: tbl-patient-characteristics",
    "#| tbl-cap: 'Patient characteristics by readmission status'",
    "# Table 1 code here (gtsummary / gt)",
    fence_end,
    "",
    "## Results",
    "",
    fence_r,
    "#| label: fig-roc-curve",
    "#| fig-cap: 'ROC curve for 30-day readmission model'",
    "#| fig-width: 8",
    "#| fig-height: 5",
    "# Figure code here (ggplot2)",
    fence_end,
    "",
    "@fig-roc-curve shows model discrimination (AUC = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.74-0.81).",
    "",
    "## References",
    "",
    "::: {#refs}",
    ":::"
  ),
  collapse = "\n"
)
cat("Quarto document template:\n")
cat(substr(QMD_TEMPLATE, 1, 1200), "\n")
qmd_path <- file.path(mod08_dir, "readmission_report.qmd")
writeLines(QMD_TEMPLATE, qmd_path)
cat("\nTemplate written to:", qmd_path, "\n")
```

## 4. Publication-Quality Figures (300 dpi)

```{r}
set.seed(42)
split <- initial_split(df, prop = 0.8, strata = readmitted)
train <- training(split)
test  <- testing(split)

fit <- glm(
  readmitted ~ age + los_days + diabetes + hf + smoking,
  data = train, family = binomial()
)
prob <- predict(fit, newdata = test, type = "response")
auc  <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(test$readmitted, prob, quiet = TRUE))
roc_obj <- pROC::roc(test$readmitted, prob, quiet = TRUE)
roc_df <- tibble(fpr = 1 - roc_obj$specificities, tpr = roc_obj$sensitivities)

# Panel A — ROC
p_a <- ggplot(roc_df, aes(fpr, tpr)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = tpr), fill = col_red, alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_line(colour = col_red, linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "1 - Specificity", y = "Sensitivity",
       title = "A  ROC Curve", subtitle = sprintf("AUC = %.3f", auc))

# Panel B — Score distribution
score_df <- tibble(prob = prob, readmitted = factor(test$readmitted,
                     labels = c("Not readmitted", "Readmitted")))
p_b <- ggplot(score_df, aes(prob, fill = readmitted)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 25, alpha = 0.65,
                 position = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(col_blue, col_red)) +
  labs(x = "Predicted probability", y = "Density",
       title = "B  Score Distribution", fill = NULL)

# Panel C — Readmission by factor
baseline <- mean(df$readmitted) * 100
factor_rates <- tibble(
  feature = c("HF", "Diabetes", "Smoking", "LOS>7d", "Age>70"),
  rate = c(
    mean(df$readmitted[df$hf == 1]),
    mean(df$readmitted[df$diabetes == 1]),
    mean(df$readmitted[df$smoking == 1]),
    mean(df$readmitted[df$los_days > 7]),
    mean(df$readmitted[df$age > 70])
  ) * 100
) %>%
  mutate(col = if_else(rate > baseline + 3, col_red, col_blue))
p_c <- ggplot(factor_rates, aes(rate, reorder(feature, rate), fill = col)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.85, colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = baseline, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  labs(x = "30-day readmission rate (%)", y = NULL,
       title = "C  Readmission by Factor")

# Panel D — Payer analysis
payer_rates <- df %>%
  group_by(payer) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(readmitted) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(rate)) %>%
  mutate(payer = factor(payer, levels = payer),
         col = c(col_red, col_gold, col_blue, col_green))
p_d <- ggplot(payer_rates, aes(payer, rate, fill = col)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.85, colour = "white") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = baseline, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", rate)), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Readmission rate (%)", title = "D  Readmission by Payer") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))

# Panel E — Feature importance (log-odds coefficients)
coefs <- broom::tidy(fit) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(col = if_else(estimate > 0, col_red, col_blue))
p_e <- ggplot(coefs, aes(estimate, reorder(term, estimate), fill = col)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.85, colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  labs(x = "Log-odds coefficient", y = NULL, title = "E  Model Coefficients")

# Panel F — LOS distribution
p_f <- ggplot(df, aes(los_days, fill = factor(readmitted,
                     labels = c("Not readmitted", "Readmitted")))) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 20, alpha = 0.6,
                 position = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(col_blue, col_red)) +
  labs(x = "Length of Stay (days)", y = "Density",
       title = "F  LOS Distribution", fill = NULL)

fig1 <- (p_a | p_b | p_c) / (p_d | p_e | p_f) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "30-Day Hospital Readmission Analysis Report",
    subtitle = "Figure 1: Key Results Summary"
  )
print(fig1)
ggsave(file.path(mod08_dir, "quarto_figure1.png"), fig1,
       width = 18, height = 10, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
cat(sprintf("Publication figure saved at 300 dpi | AUC=%.3f\n", auc))
```

## 5. Programmatic Table 1

```{r}
# Generate publication-ready Table 1 (patient characteristics)
table1_row_continuous <- function(df_all, col, group_col = "readmitted", label = NULL) {
  label <- label %||% col
  overall <- sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(df_all[[col]]), sd(df_all[[col]]))
  g0 <- df_all[[col]][df_all[[group_col]] == 0]
  g1 <- df_all[[col]][df_all[[group_col]] == 1]
  p  <- wilcox.test(g0, g1, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value
  tibble(
    Variable = label, Overall = overall,
    `Not Readmitted` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(g0), sd(g0)),
    Readmitted = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(g1), sd(g1)),
    `p-value` = sprintf("%.3f", p)
  )
}

table1_row_binary <- function(df_all, col, group_col = "readmitted", label = NULL) {
  label <- label %||% col
  overall <- sprintf("%.1f%%", mean(df_all[[col]]) * 100)
  g0 <- df_all[[col]][df_all[[group_col]] == 0]
  g1 <- df_all[[col]][df_all[[group_col]] == 1]
  ct <- table(df_all[[col]], df_all[[group_col]])
  p  <- chisq.test(ct)$p.value
  tibble(
    Variable = label, Overall = overall,
    `Not Readmitted` = sprintf("%.1f%%", mean(g0) * 100),
    Readmitted = sprintf("%.1f%%", mean(g1) * 100),
    `p-value` = sprintf("%.3f", p)
  )
}

table1 <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    Variable = "N", Overall = as.character(nrow(df)),
    `Not Readmitted` = as.character(sum(df$readmitted == 0)),
    Readmitted = as.character(sum(df$readmitted == 1)),
    `p-value` = ""
  ),
  table1_row_continuous(df, "age", "readmitted", "Age (years), mean (SD)"),
  table1_row_continuous(df, "los_days", "readmitted", "Length of stay (days), mean (SD)"),
  table1_row_binary(df, "diabetes", "readmitted", "Diabetes, n (%)"),
  table1_row_binary(df, "hf", "readmitted", "Heart failure, n (%)"),
  table1_row_binary(df, "smoking", "readmitted", "Current smoker, n (%)")
)
cat("Table 1: Patient Characteristics by Readmission Status\n")
cat(strrep("=", 75), "\n")
print(table1)
gt(table1) %>% tab_header(title = "Patient characteristics by readmission status")

write_csv(table1, file.path(mod08_dir, "table1.csv"))
cat("\nTable 1 saved to", file.path(mod08_dir, "table1.csv"), "\n")
```

## 6. Quarto Rendering Commands

```{r}
QUARTO_COMMANDS <- paste(
  c(
    "# Install Quarto (once):",
    "# wget https://quarto.org/download/latest/quarto-linux-amd64.deb",
    "# sudo dpkg -i quarto-linux-amd64.deb",
    "",
    "# Render to HTML (self-contained):",
    "# quarto render report.qmd --to html",
    "",
    "# Render to PDF (requires LaTeX):",
    "# quarto render report.qmd --to pdf",
    "",
    "# Render to Word:",
    "# quarto render report.qmd --to docx",
    "",
    "# Render all formats:",
    "# quarto render report.qmd",
    "",
    "# Preview with live reload:",
    "# quarto preview report.qmd",
    "",
    "# Publish to Quarto Pub:",
    "# quarto publish quarto-pub report.qmd",
    "",
    "# Cross-references in .qmd:",
    "# @fig-roc-curve   -> Figure 1",
    "# @tbl-table1      -> Table 1",
    "# @sec-methods     -> Section 2",
    "# @eq-logistic     -> Equation 1"
  ),
  collapse = "\n"
)
cat(QUARTO_COMMANDS, "\n")
```

## 7. Advanced Quarto Features

```{r}
QUARTO_ADVANCED <- paste(
  c(
    "## Panel Layout",
    "::: {layout-ncol=2}",
    paste0(strrep("`", 3), "{r}"),
    "#| label: fig-roc",
    "plot_roc()",
    strrep("`", 3),
    paste0(strrep("`", 3), "{r}"),
    "#| label: fig-calibration",
    "plot_calibration()",
    strrep("`", 3),
    ":::",
    "",
    "## Tabset",
    "::: {.panel-tabset}",
    "### Training Set",
    "Content for training set...",
    "### Test Set",
    "Content for test set...",
    ":::",
    "",
    "## Callout Boxes",
    "::: {.callout-warning}",
    "### Model Limitations",
    "This model was trained on a single-site cohort and may not generalise.",
    ":::",
    "",
    "::: {.callout-tip}",
    "### Clinical Application",
    "Flag patients with predicted probability > 0.30 for care transition support.",
    ":::",
    "",
    "## Conditional Content (for-loop tables)",
    paste0(strrep("`", 3), "{r}"),
    "#| output: asis",
    "for (payer in unique(df$payer)) {",
    "  sub <- df %>% filter(payer == !!payer)",
    "  cat(sprintf('### %s (n=%d)\\n', payer, nrow(sub)))",
    "  print(knitr::kable(summary(sub)))",
    "}",
    strrep("`", 3)
  ),
  collapse = "\n"
)
cat(QUARTO_ADVANCED, "\n")
```

## 8. Knowledge Check
1. What is the advantage of Quarto's `execute: cache: true` for a long-running model?
2. How do cross-references (`@fig-roc`) differ from manually typing "Figure 1"?
3. A journal requires a Word `.docx` with specific formatting. How does Quarto handle this?
4. Your `.qmd` renders fine locally but fails in CI because `quarto` is not installed. How do you fix this?
5. Build a Quarto parameterised report that generates separate HTML pages for each hospital unit.

```{r}
# Exercise 5 — Parameterised Quarto report
PARAMETERISED_QMD <- paste(
  c(
    "---",
    "title: 'Unit Report: {{< meta params.unit_name >}}'",
    "params:",
    "  unit_name: 'Cardiology'",
    "  min_date:  '2023-01-01'",
    "  max_date:  '2023-12-31'",
    "engine: knitr",
    "---",
    "",
    paste0(strrep("`", 3), "{r}"),
    "unit <- params$unit_name",
    "df_unit <- df %>% filter(unit == unit)",
    "cat(sprintf('Report for %s: N=%d patients\\n', unit, nrow(df_unit)))",
    strrep("`", 3),
    "",
    "# Render for each unit from command line:",
    "# for unit in Cardiology Pulmonology Neurology; do",
    "#   quarto render unit_report.qmd -P unit_name:$unit --output ${unit}_report.html",
    "# done"
  ),
  collapse = "\n"
)
cat("Parameterised report template:\n")
cat(PARAMETERISED_QMD, "\n")

# Simulate rendering for multiple units
units <- c("Cardiology", "Pulmonology", "Neurology")
set.seed(42)
df$unit <- sample(units, nrow(df), replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.4, 0.35, 0.25))
for (unit in units) {
  sub <- df %>% filter(unit == !!unit)
  readmit_r <- mean(sub$readmitted) * 100
  cat(sprintf("Unit: %-15s | N=%4d | Readmission rate: %.1f%%\n",
              unit, nrow(sub), readmit_r))
}
```
